open_items: ABS gateway metadata empty-error-body flap: fifth occurrence, cycles 150-152 (3 consecutive cycles, 4 hours), resolved by cycle 153, healthy through cycle 163 (no new occurrence, 12 consecutive healthy cycles). Longest occurrence yet (prior max was 2 consecutive cycles, cycles 150-151; before that all resolved within one cycle: cycle 26, cycle 134, cycle 143). Empty error message itself still worth fixing under code-change scope (GatewayError/next_step in monitor/checks_gateway.py). Watch for a sixth occurrence; if it spans 4+ cycles, treat as a genuine regression rather than the known cosmetic pattern.

ESTAT list_dataflows timeout pattern: ninth episode (cycles 144-145) resolved by cycle 146, clean through cycle 163 (18 consecutive healthy cycles). No fix applied under docs-only scope; standing recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result) carried forward for a session with code-change scope. Watch for a tenth episode, especially one that fails to resolve within a cycle or two.
STATSNZ auth:listing capability_appeared, first seen cycle 60, still present at cycle 163: listing served without credentials. Still open, not re-reported since no new change.

Content-Type parameter order (charset vs version) on structure responses varies between requests, seen on ABS, OECD, ILO, and FBOS. Cosmetic, verdict stays ok. Expected to keep flapping across multiple endpoints; do not re-report unless the verdict itself changes.

ILO direct-path 403 flap: third occurrence at cycle 159 (10:01:22Z), broadest yet - 10 of 12 contract assertions broken, resolved by cycle 160, clean through cycle 163 (no new occurrence). Prior occurrences: cycle 32, cycle 94. All three resolved within one cycle. Basic gateway/direct health checks stayed healthy throughout every occurrence - only contract-probe traffic drew the 403. IMPORTANT: /api/history's per-endpoint status/failing series does NOT reflect contract-probe-only degradation - it showed healthy/[] for ILO at cycle 159 despite the cycle being degraded, and the same blind spot recurred for IMF at cycle 161 (see below). Future runs must check /api/cycle/{id} for every intermediate cycle since the last run, not rely on /api/history or /api/contracts changes (which only diffs the two newest cycles) alone. Watch for a fourth ILO occurrence, especially one that fails to resolve within a cycle.

IMF references:* 401 flap: first occurrence, cycle 161 (14:01:22Z) - 4 of the references:* contract assertions (all, children, descendants, parentsandsiblings) returned HTTP 401 where 200 was expected, resolved by cycle 162, clean through cycle 163. Basic gateway/direct health checks stayed healthy throughout cycle 161 - only contract-probe traffic drew the 401, same shape as the recurring ILO 403 flap (probe volume tripping provider-side throttling, not a general IMF outage). Live recheck against api.imf.org several hours after the fact confirmed all four references values return 200 now. Watch for a second occurrence; a second episode soon would elevate this from one-off to a recognized pattern like ILO's.

UNICEF direct-path HTTP 429 flap at cycle 126 (direct data + direct json), resolved by cycle 127, still resolved through cycle 163 (36 more cycles clean). Watch for recurrence; a second episode soon would suggest rate-limit triggering rather than a one-off.
